parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calcium metal reacts with chlorine gas to form calcium chloride, $\text{CaCl}_2$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation, including state symbols, to represent the lattice energy of calcium chloride, $\text{CaCl}_2$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Complete a fully labelled Born-Haber cycle that could be used to calculate the lattice energy, $\Delta H^\ominus_\text{latt}$, for calcium chloride.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
Use your answer to (ii) and the following data, together with relevant data from the Data Booklet, to calculate a value for $\Delta H^\ominus_\text{latt}$ for calcium chloride.

|  |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| standard enthalpy change of formation of $\text{CaCl}_2\text{(s)}$, $\Delta H^\ominus_\text{f}$ | $-796\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| standard enthalpy change of atomisation of $\text{Ca(s)}$, $\Delta H^\ominus_\text{at}$ | $+178\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| electron affinity of chlorine atoms | $-349\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Entropy is a measure of the disorder of a system.

Describe and explain what happens to the entropy of a gas when the temperature is increased.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
For each reaction, predict the sign of the entropy change, $\Delta S^\ominus$. If you predict no entropy change, write 'no change' in the table below. The first one has been done for you.

| reaction | sign of $\Delta S^\ominus$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{CO}\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$ | negative |
| $\text{Mg}\text{(s)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{MgO}\text{(s)}$ |  |
| $\text{CuSO}_4\text{(s)} + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} \rightarrow \text{CuSO}_4.5\text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(s)}$ |  |
| $\text{NaHCO}_3\text{(s)} + \text{H}^+\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)}$ |  |

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the entropy change for the first process is negative.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Calculate the standard entropy change, $\Delta S^\ominus$, for this reaction.

$$\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$$

Standard entropies, $S^\ominus$, in $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ are given.

| $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ | $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ | $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| +192 | +131 | +193 |

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Whether or not a chemical reaction is spontaneous (feasible) can be deduced by calculating the change in free energy, $\Delta G^\ominus$, at a given temperature.

$$\text{MgCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{MgO}\text{(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

$\Delta H^\ominus = +117\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta S^\ominus = +175\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the value of $\Delta G^\ominus$ at $298\text{ K}$ for the above reaction.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer to (i) to explain whether or not this reaction is spontaneous at $298\text{ K}$.
